title: Golden Criterion Adaptive Equal-Weight vs Optimized Blend for H026 ETF Rotation
source: arXiv:2607.11054 (Jul 2026) — "When and Why Naive Diversification Works: A Simple Diagnostic Strategy" (Feng, Huang, Wang, Zhang)
description: The paper proves that equal-weighting (1/N) is minimum-variance optimal when the forecast-error covariance matrix has uniform eigenstructure (the 'Golden Criterion'). The two-stage adaptive strategy dynamically blends 1/N weights and optimized (MV/momentum) weights based on empirical distance from this uniform-eigenstructure condition. H478 adapts this to the H026 25-ETF universe: measure whether the cross-sectional momentum signal has approximately uniform predictive error covariance (i.e., the top-1 momentum winner is no more reliably identified than any other top-3) and, if so, switch from concentrated top-1 to equal-weight top-3 selection. This directly tests whether the H026 top-1 concentration (which drives its high Sharpe) remains justified when momentum signal quality degrades.
content_summary: Paper identifies 'Golden Criterion': equal weighting is minimum-variance optimal iff the forecast-error covariance matrix Σ_e has a uniform eigenstructure (all eigenvalues equal). Empirically, the method computes the distance from uniform eigenstructure as D = ||λ - λ_mean||_2 / ||λ||_2 where λ are eigenvalues of Σ_e. When D < threshold (close to uniform), 1/N weights are optimal; when D > threshold (concentrated errors), optimized weights (including concentrated momentum pick) win. Applied to U.S. equity premium forecasting: method delivers consistent OOS Sharpe gains from this regime-dependent weighting. H026 adaptation: (a) at each monthly rebalance, compute the eigenstructure of the 12-month trailing return covariance matrix for the top-k ETFs by momentum score; (b) if D < D_threshold (IS-calibrated): use equal-weight of top-3; (c) if D >= D_threshold (concentrated, signal is reliable): use top-1. Rationale: H026 degrades when momentum is noisy (2022-2026 OOS ~0.785 vs IS ~1.2). The Golden Criterion provides an IS-calibrated mechanism to detect when momentum is in its noisy phase and switch to diversified allocation. Var C tests the theoretical complement: always equal-weight top-3 (ignoring criterion), providing a performance floor. Compare to H346 OB-gated version.
variants: Var A: Golden Criterion gate — top-1 when D > D_threshold, EW top-3 when D <= D_threshold
Var B: Var A but with D threshold at 50th IS percentile (more aggressive switching)
Var C: Always EW top-3 (ignoring criterion, benchmark for diversification alone)
Var D: Always EW top-5 (more diversified)
Var E: H026 canonical top-1 baseline
gate: OOS Sharpe > 2.610 (H346 OB-gated baseline) AND MaxDD improvement vs -5%
data_requirements: yfinance daily ETF prices for H026 25-asset universe (already in production). No additional data needed. Golden Criterion distance computed from trailing 12m monthly return covariance matrix of top-k ETFs by momentum rank.
implementation_notes: Golden Criterion distance implementation: (1) at monthly rebalance date, take trailing 12m monthly returns for top-5 ETFs by 12m momentum rank; (2) compute 5x5 covariance matrix Sigma; (3) eigendecompose: lambdas = np.linalg.eigvalsh(Sigma); (4) D = np.std(lambdas) / np.mean(lambdas) (coefficient of variation — simpler than L2 distance, proportional); (5) IS-calibrate D_threshold as median D over 2008-2017; (6) if D < D_threshold → EW top-3; else → top-1. CAUTION: small sample (12 monthly returns for 5 ETFs) means eigenvalue estimation is noisy. Use regularization: Sigma_reg = 0.9*Sigma + 0.1*np.trace(Sigma)/n*np.eye(n). Hypothesis is that when the top ETFs have similar 12m returns (uniform covariance eigenstructure), picking a single winner is unreliable — switch to diversification. When one ETF clearly dominates (concentrated eigenstructure), momentum signal is reliable — use top-1. This is a principled version of what H273 (vol-targeting) and H346 (OB filter) do implicitly.
